title: ax.config.json
description: Per-project configuration for the ax CLI. Every value that used to be hardcoded in a project's worktree scripts lives here.

name.description: Slug used for Docker project ids, Portless hostnames and log tags.

dev.description: Inclusive band a worktree's dev port is allocated from.

step.description: Port offset between two isolated Supabase stacks.

maxSlot.description: How many isolated Supabase blocks exist. Slot n uses supabaseBase + n*step, so the last block must still fit under the top of the reserved Supabase range.

reserved.description: Ports and ranges never allocated, e.g. "3000" or "54320-59999".

web.description: Application root whose env and runtime files ax manages. Defaults to the repository root.

e2e.description: Path to the end-to-end test workspace, when the repository has one.

caches.description: Extra workspace roots whose generated test/build output a worktree cleanup reclaims.

repo.description: owner/name of the upstream kit. Matched against remote URLs, never against a remote name.

guarded.description: Trees shared with the vendor. Value is "vendor" (all theirs) or two explicit lists.

oneOf.description: Both lists are explicit so a path added later belongs to neither and gets flagged.

debugAs.description: Adopt project debug sessions explicitly: declare browser and identities, plus optional phone. AX opens one visible Chromium session on this checkout's loopback application address and shares its CDP connection with agents. No defaults materialize this contract. Migration: the retired { route, optInEnv } shape is no longer a debug-session contract; remove it or replace it with this declaration. AX reports that repair without blocking version pinning and never infers identities or converts the old route into a provider.

browser.description: Where AX resolves Playwright and Chromium from, and how this application is started. AX never installs a browser and never starts the app: it names the start command as the repair when nothing answers.

playwrightDir.description: Repo-relative package that pins Playwright — `@playwright/test` or `playwright` — and whose version's device catalog `--device` reads.

start.description: The argv that starts this application, named as a repair and never executed by AX.

navigationTimeoutSeconds.description: How long the first navigation may take before the launch refuses. Required, and defaulted nowhere: a cold first compile of a privileged route routinely exceeds Playwright's own 30s, and a refusal here leaves no receipt, so the number is this project's to state.

prepare.description: The Debug adapter: the project's own way to make an authentication artifact fresh. AX passes it versioned JSON on stdin and reads one JSON object back; it never learns the login flow.

command.description: Argv, never a shell string, run from the worktree root.

timeoutSeconds.description: The adapter's deadline, required wherever an adapter is declared and defaulted nowhere. It must exceed the project's own authentication-setup budget: a cap equal to the inner test timeout kills the adapter before it can report its own failure.

phone.description: The optional Phone handoff half. Declaring it adopts the capability for this project; each identity still declares whether it supports it. Absent means the Role browser is the whole feature here.

optInEnv.description: The variable that must resolve true before an automatic handoff runs. A name only: AX reads the value from the environment and the project's local env files, never from this file.

oneOf.description: The built-in Supabase provider: the documented Auth Admin link-generation call, made directly so AX stays dependency-free.

urlEnv.description: Variable naming the Supabase URL. Loopback by default; any other host needs a machine-private allowlist entry and HTTPS.

serviceRoleKeyEnv.description: Variable naming the service-role key. The value never enters this file, a receipt, or a child process AX spawns.

confirm.description: This application's own auth callback, described so AX can build the URL with validated parameter names instead of a free-form template.

path.description: Absolute path of the callback route.

oneOf.description: The escape hatch: any other provider, through the same bounded adapter protocol. It must return a final URL on this worktree's own Tailscale origin.

identities.description: The closed catalog of Debug identities, keyed by the name `--as` takes. Closed because a filename cannot establish intent: AX never infers an identity from a fixture, a package shape or a MakerKit convention. Names and capability closure are refused with a repair by src/debug-as/config.mjs — a keyed map cannot pattern its own keys without a keyword this validator refuses by name.

defaultPath.description: Where this identity lands with no `--path`. An absolute path component of this application, never a URL; the full safety rule and its repair live in src/debug-as/config.mjs.

browser.description: Present when this identity is authenticated. Absent declares an unauthenticated identity, which needs no adapter.

storageState.description: Repo-relative Playwright storage state. AX proves it is private, ignored, inside the worktree and scoped to this checkout's own addresses; the adapter owns its freshness and its mode.

phone.description: Present when this identity supports Phone handoff. Requires the project-level `phone` section and an authenticated identity.

email.description: The account the provider mints a one-shot login for.

triage.description: What `ax triage` has to know about THIS project to put a session in front of an issue. The noun names the activity: triage is the ON-RAMP, the pass for work that arrived from outside — a human report, another agent’s finding, a follow-up born during a wave. The spec chain never enters this surface, because `to-tickets` publishes its own tickets `ready-for-agent` itself. A child mutates nothing: it writes a draft, and you publish it — so what a project declares here is the vocabulary that draft has to speak.

labels.description: Path to this project's label mapping — repo-relative, or absolute when shared. It names the groups a finished triage has to fill, which `skill://triage` does not carry: left to the skill alone a session recommends in prose and stops, and on 2026-08-10 four issues landed with three empty groups each while the maintainer did the data entry. Absent or unreadable is a refusal for the jobs that apply labels: `gh label list` enumerates names but knows nothing about groups or completeness, so a child dispatched without this is under-specified before it starts.

provenance.description: Whether a ticket's ORIGIN forbids the pass you asked for, named with labels this project already applies. `spec` names the labels meaning 'born from a spec': the tickets your own spec flow produced, which `to-tickets` already published as `ready-for-agent` and quizzed with you in the room — so a triage or brief pass over one is REFUSED, because it would re-decide a categorization its spec already fixed, and because there is no other pass to send it to. `inbound` names the labels meaning 'came from outside': a human's report, a follow-up born during a wave — a claim of unknown quality, which is the only work a triage pass is for. `findings` names the labels meaning 'your own agents filed this while working': inbound by provenance, arriving with its measurement (the friction contract: argv, raw output, expected state, cost), so the finder is the verifier and a triage or brief pass over one is REFUSED unless the issue itself names the approved Spec obligation it serves (`Necessary for: #<spec> — <obligation>`) — without that line the repair names the channel that owns what was found, never another pass, and admission to a pass is not authorization to implement. Absent means nothing is gated: an undeclared vocabulary is never an inferred one, and a project that tracks provenance some other way keeps routing exactly as before. Two classes on one ticket is a contradiction, refused without picking a side.

spec.description: Labels meaning this ticket was born from a spec, and is therefore agent-ready by construction. The parent sub-issue link is read too, but it decides nothing on its own: nesting proves nesting, and a follow-up nested under its origin ticket is inbound.

inbound.description: Labels meaning this ticket came from outside as a claim to verify: a human report, or a follow-up born during a wave. The triage lane is for these.

findings.description: Labels meaning your own agents filed this ticket while working, with its measurement attached. A triage or brief pass runs over one only when the issue itself names the approved Spec obligation it serves (`Necessary for: #<spec> — <obligation>`); without that line a maintainer answers it with a verdict comment when it is in the instrument, `to-tickets` publishes it when it is in the product. An unreadable justification is not treated as present. Declare it to opt in; leave it absent to keep such tickets in the triage lane.

dispatch.description: What `ax worker dispatch` has to know about THIS project to turn a ticket into a dispatched session. Every value here replaced a constant that used to be hardcoded for one repository — so nothing here carries a default, with ONE exception named at `cap`: a floor measured for one fleet, inherited by a repo that never declared it, is the same bug in a new place. What a project does not declare is not measured, and the report says so.

cap.description: How many live child panes THIS repository may hold at once, counted from the dispatch records that name it — per REPOSITORY and never per checkout, so a linked worktree and its primary checkout share one cap. Enforced by `ax worker dispatch` and `ax triage dispatch` alike, and printed by `ax worker ls`. Absent means 3, the one defaulted key in this block: a cap that binds only where somebody declared it does not bind, which is what #88 measured — the store is host-global, so before this key the only count anything could read was machine-wide, and a 13-issue wave here ran at one slot while another checkout held two panes. It is a fairness number rather than a measurement of any machine's appetite, which is what makes a default safe here where a memory floor's would not be. Zero is legal and stops every new pane for this repository. A record naming no repository is UNKNOWN and counts toward machineCap alone (F-028). The default lives in `src/worker/capacity.mjs` (REPO_CAP_DEFAULT), its only reader.

machineCap.description: A ceiling on EVERY live child pane on this machine, whoever owns it — the fuse, not the fairness mechanism. Absent means there is no ceiling at all: it does not exist until an operator declares it, and that absence is the behaviour #88 ruled for, because an unset ceiling that still meant 3 (the old ORCA_TRIAGE_SESSION_CAP default) let another checkout's panes eat the fuse while this repository never reached its own cap. Declare it where the machine has a real shared limit — Orca's long-poll cap is 16 — and both dispatch verbs refuse against it, naming both numbers and which cap refused. It is also the BOUND that lets a checkout `gh` cannot name dispatch at all: without a name there is no per-repository count to gate, and an unmeasurable cap authorizes nothing (F-028), so this ceiling is what makes such a mutation bounded rather than ungated. Declared per project even though it is a fact about the machine: whoever arms the fuse arms it from the checkout they dispatch from, and `ax worker ls` prints the declaration it read. Both retired env knobs, ORCA_TRIAGE_SESSION_CAP and ORCA_READY_SESSION_CAP, are refused by name in favour of this key.

entry.description: The instruction a child is given when --task is not passed — the entry point that decides what it does with the ticket. Absent means every dispatch must pass --task: ax cannot invent the verb a project's agents answer to.

contract.description: Path to the pilot contract appended to every brief — repo-relative, or absolute for a contract shared by several repos. Declared and unreadable is a refusal: a brief pointing at nothing sends a child to improvise (2026-08-01, three worktrees that never read theirs). Absent means ax writes the mechanics-only contract it owns. Declared, it REPLACES those mechanics rather than adding to them, so it has to re-carry whatever they said that nothing else in this repo tells a child: the provisioned worktree and its `.agent/worktree-context.local.md`, who the orchestrator is, that the child never merges, and the stall watcher. A contract that drops a verification sequence because the repo's AGENTS.md carries it is deduplicating; the same contract copied into a repo whose AGENTS.md does not is losing it.

worktreeTool.description: The repo's own worktree creator, when it has one. It must BLOCK until the tree is usable and print the path on its last stdout line — absolute, or relative to the directory the dispatch ran in, which ax resolves. Absent means Orca places the worktree and `ax worktree setup` provisions it.

databaseLabels.description: Tracker labels that mean 'this ticket touches the database'. A dispatch carrying one of them provisions its worktree with its own Supabase stack (`ax worktree setup --database`) instead of letting the plan decide from a diff — and the diff of a tree that was created seconds ago is empty, so an issue whose whole subject is the database was provisioned to SHARE the primary checkout's stack. Measured 2026-08-25 on ofmchat #71 (domain:database, domain:security): the brief required an isolated reset and a full pgTAP run, and the worktree was announced as not touching the database. Absent means no ticket label forces isolation and the plan decides alone; the guard in front of `ax supabase` still promotes on the first write, but only for commands that go through it.

hosts.description: Execution hosts this project may dispatch to, keyed by the Orca environment name passed to --on. A host absent from here cannot be dispatched to, and a ground it does not declare is not measured — the floors are what keep a newcomer from being OOM-killed for an incumbent's appetite, and they are per host and per project footprint.

ssh.description: ssh target that reaches this host, for the grounds Orca cannot answer.

diskPath.description: Mount point the worktrees land on — a remote worktree installs its own dependencies. Measured only together with diskFloorGb.

diskFloorGb.description: Free gigabytes below which a dispatch onto this host is refused. Measured only together with diskPath.

cgroup.description: cgroup directory of the unit every session on that host shares. Measured only together with memFreeFloorMb.

memFreeFloorMb.description: Unreclaimable headroom below which a dispatch is refused — never `memory.current`, which counts page cache the kernel drops under pressure. Measured only together with cgroup.

sweep.description: argv run on the host before memory is measured, to reclaim browsers an earlier stage left open. Refusing over dead renderers is a refusal about garbage. `ax worker sweep --apply --under <dir>` is that verb: it names the paths it owns, judges a browser by the AGE OF ITS ROOT, and exits 0 whatever it finds so a sweep is never why a dispatch stops.

sessions.description: Session transcript root on that host, so the marker check crosses the transport unchanged instead of degrading into a weaker one.

prGate.description: What `ax pr gate` must be able to decide before a merge. The Bash this replaces kept one machine-wide file keyed by owner/repo, because it was a machine-wide script; this key lives in the checkout it is about, so the repo name is not part of it. An ABSENT prGate is not `nothing expected, therefore nothing missing`: the gate cannot establish anything and says so.

$comment.description: Why THIS expectation and not another. Kept in the file rather than in a commit message because the reasoning is what a later reader needs before changing the value: which job aggregates what, which one is deliberately absent, and what a green verdict therefore does not cover.

aggregate.description: The ONE check-run name whose verdict covers this repository's CI. Use it where a single job aggregates the rest: the set of runs on a SHA depends on the diff, on labels and on bots that decide for themselves whether to run — 21 on one PR and 15 on another an hour apart (F-014), so counting them proves nothing.

checks.description: The check-run names that must each be green, for a repository with no aggregate job. Every name must have a COMPLETED run whose conclusion is success on the exact head SHA; a name with no run at all is a refusal, not an absence. The gate looks for them over EVERY page of that SHA's check-run list, reconciled against the total the endpoint announces, so a name is never missed for sitting past the first hundred rows and a later re-run concluding failure is not hidden by an earlier green row of the same name (#176). A complete read is not an atomic snapshot: runs created while it paginates belong to the next run of the gate.

residualFindings.description: Repository-relative directory holding residual review findings, if this project keeps one. Declared rather than assumed: the Bash hardcoded `docs/residual-review-findings`, which is one project's layout living in a tool. Absent means that ground is not run, and the gate says so instead of passing it.

release.description: The shape of THIS project's release pull request, on which the closing-keyword ground answers `no ticket by construction`, the commits-since-open detector expects the version bump, and ticket binding is not run. Absent means the default shape: author `github-actions[bot]` carrying the label `autorelease: pending`, which is what release-please writes. Declared REPLACES that default — the label a project does not declare stops opening the exemption. Measured on PR #68: the keyword ground refused every release PR structurally, and `.github/workflows/test.yml` promises the release path stays gateable.

$comment.description: Why this project's release PR looks like this — which automation opens it, and what labels that automation writes.

label.description: The label the release automation puts on its own pull request, e.g. `autorelease: pending`. Required: a label with no release author would be a flag any contributor could add, so both halves are read.

author.description: The login the release automation runs as. Absent means `github-actions[bot]`. Both `app/<slug>` and `<slug>[bot]` spellings of one App match: gh answers the first on `pr view --json author` and the second on the commits endpoint.

tracker.description: The tracker this project's issues live in, when they do not live in GitHub. Both halves or neither: a name with no pattern cannot find a ref, and a pattern with no name cannot say what it found.

$comment.description: Why this project's issues do not live in GitHub, so a later reader does not delete the key as redundant.

name.description: Human name of the tracker, e.g. Linear — printed so the reader knows where the ticket is.

pattern.description: Regular expression matching one of its refs, e.g. `GAP-[0-9]+`. Measured 2026-08-16: without this, the gate printed `the body closes no issue and expresses no intent to` on three PRs that each carried `Fixes GAP-3xx` — the issues were disabled on GitHub and lived in Linear.
